evidence.controls: Four native child controls pass protected 32/64-bit read/write capture under the guest Linux ARM64 x7 entry/exit protocol. VerifyNative independently decodes instructions and effective addresses. LLVM 23.1.1, LLD 23.1.1, helper ELF and Linux v3.18 ABI references are pinned in experiments/xdma-native/inputs.toml. Native C/assembly is confined to the ptrace ABI boundary; Kotlin verifies evidence.
evidence.stock-capture: docs/research/xdma-native.md SHA-256 9be11e144613e016f0bb3d2b29e42afbe6e228c9eee821e42274dbccf6ec3782 records the exact original mmap tuple and call site, protected anonymous substitution, kernel mapping return and complete first fault: read32 at offset 0x4048, stock PC 0x270604 opcode b9400109. Native registers, siginfo and independent debuggerd stack corroborate the access and identify its caller as DevSystemSCU_GetFPGADNA. No read response was supplied.
evidence.integrity: experiments/xdma-native/results.toml SHA-256 e53918b9d92a2193cdb4f8aebe5363a29be916b93e5892d2d4a400e80642548a pins the immutable raw run, native binary, source and verification. VerifyNative passed APK/native hashes, signers, shared UID, process label, admission negative controls and stable system_server PID 1068. No Frida in stock process maps; guest enforcing remains. An earlier root Binder-thread crash is separately disclosed with unknown process identity, not attributed to MMIO. Guest and isolated listeners are gone. No host security changes or physical instrument access.
